title: kv-cache: adaptive fragmentation-aware eviction + paging spillover heuristics (v24)
author: Olivia Chen
release_notes: Improves KV cache memory management: adaptive fragmentation scoring, smarter paging thresholds, and safer spillover compaction. Reduces p99 token latency under memory pressure and decreases OOM-related request failures.
description: Context: Production serving nodes occasionally hit high fragmentation in the KV cache which leads to premature spillover, increased page churn, and higher p99 latencies under tail workloads. This PR implements a conservative, adaptive eviction policy that accounts for fragmentation score, request affinity, and temporal locality before triggering paging/spillover. Summary: Adds fragmentation-aware scoring to the eviction pipeline, defers aggressive compaction by predicting re-use windows, exposes tunable paging thresholds, and improves spillover compaction to coalesce adjacent pages before writing to backing store. Includes scheduler hints to avoid evicting KV entries currently used by in-flight batches. Design highlights: - Fragmentation score: lightweight estimator (bitmap-based) computed per slab to prefer eviction of highly fragmented regions. - Reuse window prediction: short-lived tokens are protected by a decay-based hotness multiplier to prevent thrashing during bursts. - Paging thresholds: dynamically adjusted based on free slab ratio and recent paging latency. - Spillover compaction: adjacent page coalescing to reduce IO amplification and improve rehydration cost. - Scheduling integration: eviction requests include a soft affinity tag; scheduler avoids eviction during continuous-batching windows where KV entries are likely hot. Testing & validation: Unit tests for scoring and heuristics, e2e perf canary against a mixed-length chat workload, and stress runs simulating fragmentation growth. Canary results show 18% improvement in p99 generation latency under synthetic fragmentation scenarios and 32% reduction in paging IO. Migration & tunables: New config keys (kv.eviction.fragmentation_score_enabled, kv.eviction.paging_thresholds, kv.spillover.coalesce_window_ms) with conservative defaults matching current behavior. Backwards-compatible: feature gated off by default for private deployments and rolled out by default in hosted with a staged canary. Motivation & impact: This targets incidents where tail workloads suffer due to high fragmentation and frequent spillovers. The changes are production-focused and aim to reduce latency spikes and OOM risk without increasing average latency. References: ENG-4123 (kv-cache fragmentation incidents), prior heuristic PRs v17..v23 for incremental history.

review_comments: Diego Marquez: Left a few nits on naming and one question about atomicity in the fragmentation bitmap update - can the hot path update the bitmap without a full lock?
Olivia Chen: Reply: bitmap updates use an atomic word OR and a per-slab write barrier; added a comment and benchmark showing sub-2% overhead on hot path.
Samira Gupta: Please add a safety limit so coalescing doesn't stall spillover under extreme memory pressure.
Olivia Chen: Added a coalesce_window_ms upper bound and a fallback path that writes pages uncoalesced when queue latency exceeds threshold.
Ethan Brooks: Approve after CI fixes. Question on metrics: we should track coalesce rate and average rehydration time.
Olivia Chen: Added kv.cache.spillover.coalesce_count and kv.cache.spillover.rehydration_ms metrics to the PR.
